learning_objective: 🎯 Bridge the gap between algebra and geometry! Learn to calculate distances on a graph and find coordinates of points that divide line segments.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A graph grid with an x-axis (horizontal) and a y-axis (vertical). A point is written as (x, y). The x-coordinate is the abscissa, and the y-coordinate is the ordinate.
To find the distance between two points A(x1, y1) and B(x2, y2), we use the formula derived from Pythagoras Theorem: AB = √[(x2 - x1)² + (y2 - y1)²].
The distance of any point P(x, y) from the origin O(0, 0) is a simpler version of the formula: OP = √(x² + y²).
To find the coordinates of a point P(x, y) that divides a line segment joining A(x1, y1) and B(x2, y2) in the ratio m1 : m2, we use: x = (m1x2 + m2x1)/(m1 + m2) and y = (m1y2 + m2y1)/(m1 + m2).
A special case of the section formula where the ratio is 1:1. The midpoint is simply the average of the coordinates: x = (x1 + x2)/2 and y = (y1 + y2)/2.

fun_activity.title: 🗺️ The Treasure Map
fun_activity.instructions: Draw a graph on paper. Plot your House at (1, 2) and a Hidden Treasure at (4, 6). Use the distance formula to figure out exactly how many 'units' you need to walk to reach the gold!

exam_tips: 📌 To prove three points are collinear (on the same straight line), show that the sum of distances of two smaller segments equals the longest segment (e.g., AB + BC = AC).
📌 When a point is on the x-axis, its coordinates are (x, 0). When a point is on the y-axis, its coordinates are (0, y). Use this to solve for unknown ratios!
📌 Be extremely careful with negative signs when subtracting coordinates inside the square brackets of the distance formula (e.g., x2 - (-x1) becomes x2 + x1).
quick_recap: ⭐ Rene Descartes is the mathematician who created coordinate geometry to solve geometrical problems using algebra.
⭐ The section formula gives the exact location of a point dividing a line from the inside (internal division).
⭐ The distance formula is essentially the Pythagorean theorem applied to a coordinate plane.
